seo_title: Cost of Living in Sousse 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Sousse per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: A resort on Tunisia's Mediterranean coast: visa-free entry for 90 days, a mild climate, a UNESCO-protected medina and affordable prices. The downsides — the seasonal nature of the resort and the prevalence of French over English.
pros: Visa-free for 90 days for Russian citizens
A mild Mediterranean climate and beaches
cons: The seasonal nature of the resort — quieter in winter
French is more widespread than English

visa_steps.title: Visa-free entry
visa_steps.description: Russians enjoy visa-free stays of up to 90 days — all you need is a passport.

visa_steps.title: Renting a home
visa_steps.description: Seaside apartments are rented monthly and are cheaper out of season.

visa_steps.title: Connectivity and money
visa_steps.description: A local SIM card is cheap; you'll need dinars in cash and a foreign bank card.

visa_steps.description: Through employment, business or long-term residence you obtain a carte de séjour.

visa_steps.title: Transport

faq.question: Do Russian citizens need a visa for Sousse?
faq.answer: No, visa-free for up to 90 days. For long-term residence you apply for a residence permit.

faq.question: How much does it cost to live in Sousse?
faq.answer: Cheap, especially out of season. The exact budget is in the calculator above.

faq.question: Which language is spoken in Sousse?
faq.answer: Arabic and French; English is found in tourism.

faq.question: Can I pay with a Russian card in Sousse?
faq.answer: No, Russian cards don't work. You'll need dinars in cash and a foreign bank card.

faq.question: What is the climate like in Sousse?
faq.answer: Mediterranean: hot dry summers and mild rainy winters.

faq.question: Can you spend the winter there?
faq.answer: Yes, but in winter the resort quiets down and many things operate on a reduced schedule.

reviews.text: Sousse is a warm sea, the medina and dirt-cheap prices. In winter the resort empties out and you need French more than English, but for summer and autumn it's great.
A calm seaside town with history. Visa-free entry and low prices are the main pluses. The downsides — the seasonality and healthcare; for anything serious it's better to go to the capital.
